lead: Tacoma plumbing deals with rain, old homes, big trees and earthquake rules. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Tacoma.
risk: root-filled sewer laterals, old galvanized pipes and wet crawl spaces
risk_short: sewer roots, old pipes and wet crawl spaces
why: The North End, the Stadium District and Hilltop have homes from the 1890s to the 1940s with galvanized supply lines and clay sewer laterals. Roots from mature trees break into those lines.
Months of rain strain crawl-space drainage and sump pumps. Tacoma sits in an earthquake zone, so strapped water heaters matter.
water: Tacoma Water gets most of its water from the Green River in the Cascades, plus wells. The water is soft.
tips: Scope the sewer line before buying an older home.
Strap your water heater for earthquakes.
Check crawl-space drainage before the rainy season.
Disconnect hoses before the first freeze.
areas: PipeMend works in the North End, the Stadium District, Hilltop, Proctor, South Tacoma, the Eastside, Old Town and every other Tacoma neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from Tacoma Planning and Development Services, and plumbers must hold a certificate from the Washington State Department of Labor and Industries.

faq.q: Where does Tacoma's water come from?
faq.a: Most of it comes from the Green River watershed in the Cascades, with wells used in summer. The water is soft, so scale is rare.
